description:
Most restaurants spend money trying to make strangers notice them — ads, discounts, offers, noise. This one started after the stranger had already walked in. It treated the first visit as the most fragile moment in the business: before habit exists, before loyalty exists, before the customer has any reason to remember the place.

So the free meal was not the strategy; it was the first move in a sequence that made the customer feel chosen, rewarded, and pulled back before the memory went cold. That is the part most restaurants miss: real marketing is not just getting people through the door, it is making sure the first door they open does not become the last.
